title: senior-sync-scratchpad
content:
Context / goal:
- Prep for weekly senior team sync (30–45m). Align on 3 priorities we can commit to and 2 escalation questions for GTM/Finance. Leave time for a 10m decision.

Quick snapshot to read before the call (2 min):
- Revenue run-rate: tracking to plan; small shortfall in MRR growth vs bookings (see RI-2345).
- Hosting capacity: Dedicated pool utilization creeping up 78% during peak — risk to latency SLO if not addressed.
- Private pipeline: 2 deals near-term (legal review), 1 high-touch POC; dependency on on-prem installer fix.

Attendees (confirm): Ava (facilitator), CEO (TBD), Rajiv (Product), Emily (Finance), Jonah (Infra), Claire (Sales lead, 10m slot), Ops rep (optional).

Proposed agenda (30–45m):
1) 00:00–03:00 quick context + one-line metrics (Ava)
2) 03:00–12:00 Priorities deep-dive (pick 3): Dedicated capacity ops plan; Private deployment legal blockers; GTM enablement for new pricing tiers (owners present)
   - ask each owner: 60s status, 2 blockers, 1 decision needed
3) 12:00–22:00 Decision slot: Approve spend for short-term burst pool (cost estimate vs SLA risk)
4) 22:00–30:00 Sales highlight + ask (Claire)
5) 30:00–35:00 Escalations / risks (open mic)
6) 35:00–45:00 Parking lot + quick recaps and action assignments

Prep notes for owners (send these in Slack before meeting):
- Rajiv: bring rollout plan for Dedicated autoscaling policy; 3 options with tradeoffs and rough cost delta. Link to draft: github PR 78.
- Jonah: show current pool utilization graph + what to expect if we enable 2x burst for 48h. Need worst-case latency estimate and infra-cost delta.
- Emily: short note on budget headroom for approved burst + how that maps to next quarter forecast.
- Claire: 2-slide articulate customer asks and contract blockers; be ready to state timeline to close.

Decisions we likely need to make (prep language):
- Approve short-term burst (48h) from Dedicated reserved capacity vs force failover to hosted models. Criteria: latency risk >30% SLA breach window OR expected cost < $XXk.
- Accept revised pricing floor for dedicated monthly commits (Finance gives delta).

Open questions / things to surface to CEO:
- How aggressive do we want pricing promos for small customers this quarter (affects MR and unit economics)?
- Authorize hiring freeze exception for 1 infra contractor to expedite on-prem installer fix?

Follow-up action items (pre-fill; will confirm owners during meeting):
- Action A1: Finalize autoscale policy options and recommended default. Owner: Rajiv. Due: 2026-03-12. Jira: RI-2345.
- Action A2: Run bursting cost simulation and SLO impact matrix; include 95th/99th latency. Owner: Jonah. Due: 2026-03-11.
- Action A3: Finance to model impact of burst window on monthly P&L and marginal cost per token. Owner: Emily. Due: 2026-03-13.
- Action A4: Sales to produce redline summary for 2 in-flight private deals (legal blockers + ETA). Owner: Claire. Due: 2026-03-09.
- Action A5: Draft exec note for CEO summarizing recommended decision and risks (Ava). Due: 2026-03-11.

Notes-to-self / rough talking points:
- Keep decision framing simple: cost vs availability. Use 1 slide: chart of latency trend + cost brackets.
- Avoid technical deep-dive — if infra needs >10m, schedule separate SRE deep-dive.
- If CEO pushes for cheaper promos, push back with unit economics chart (show routing and caching levers).

Parking lot / later topics:
- Longer-term: re-architecting prefix cache to reduce peak token compute (Q3).
- Deep-dive: quantization matrix and customer-perceived quality regressions after Q2 rollouts.

Scratch (things to remember while prepping):
- Pull last week’s incident postmortem link (Slack thread thread #incidents-03).
- Update the OKR board before the meeting so we can point to progress.
- Bring one short customer quote to illustrate impact of latency on renewal.

Rough timeline for post-meeting cadence:
- Within 24h: publish short decisions + owners (Ava).
- Within 72h: owners to post progress in #exec-sync-updates (weekly checkpoint).

Random notes / incomplete thoughts (leave these):
- Could we offer a temporary credits program for affected customers while we add burst capacity? (Pros: customer goodwill; Cons: revenue leakage)
- If burst is approved, add auto-notify in Console to customers affected by degraded performance (quick UX ask).

End of scratchpad. Save this as the working copy; will copy into Confluence if the meeting notes are final.

References / quick links again:
- OKRs: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/LEAD/Leadership+Quarterly+OKRs
- Ticket: https://redwoodinference.atlassian.net/browse/RI-2345
- Draft policy PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/roadmap/pull/78
- Slack thread: slack://channel?team=T12345&id=C08ABCDEF
